title: The Poorest Man in Town Left $2 Million. How?
description:
Walter was the school janitor. Same mop, same coat with eleven safety pins, soup every night. When he died, his will left $2,032,554 to the town library and the children's hospital. How? His neighbor Lily gets a key to box 467, and inside are the clues: a notebook, a 1987 crash newspaper, 467 envelopes, and a birthday card with her name on it. A money mystery for the whole family.

The real numbers behind the story:
- $300 every month from Jan 1988 to Nov 2026 (467 months, $140,100) into an S&P 500 index fund with dividends reinvested, plus $5,000 at each of three crash lows: Oct 9, 2002 (now $73,299), Mar 9, 2009 (now $74,227) and Mar 23, 2020 (now $17,827). Total put in $155,100; worth $2,032,554 on Nov 23, 2026 (before fees and taxes).
- Balance in Nov 1996: $66,440; Nov 2006: $209,040; Nov 2016: $479,188. 76% of the money appeared in the last 10 years.
- Black Monday, Oct 19, 1987: the S&P 500 fell 20.5% in one day.
- $1,000 invested on June 1, 1998 is worth $11,063 today.
- Real people have done this: in 2014 a Vermont janitor left about $8 million, much of it to his town's library and hospital (widely reported in 2015).

Could you live like Walter for 10 years? Yes or no?

Data: S&P 500 Total Return index (Yahoo Finance ^SP500TR); S&P 500 daily closes (Yahoo Finance ^GSPC).

Walter, Lily and Derek are made up; the market returns are real. Past results don't promise future returns. Education only, not financial advice.
